title: Quantifiers 2
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty shell. 30 items, inside the 24-40 band. AN OPEN CLOZE UNIT, second on this lane, built to codex/FCE-EXERCISES.md: every gap is a quantifier, tagged `gap_class: "quantifier"`, distractors are other quantifiers and nothing else (B6), Type carries no scaffold. Four predecessors own the basics and none is repeated: a2_quantifiers (52) has much/many/a lot/few/little, a1_some_any and a2_some_any_no have some/any/no, and a2_countable has the countable split. What they do NOT have is the two things that actually separate B2 from A2 here. First, the bigger quantifiers and their countability (plenty of, a great deal of against a large number of, a couple of, several, hardly any, none of against neither of, most of, each against every, either against neither) — twelve items, each with the cue that forces exactly one answer, because several of these pairs are otherwise interchangeable and A0 would fail. Second, and this is the unit's reason to exist: **a few against few, a little against little**. Dropping the article reverses the meaning — *a few friends* is content, *few friends* is lonely — and Czech has no articles at all, so a learner drops it without hearing the difference. Every one of those twelve items carries a second clause that forces the reading (*so I am happy*, *and feels lonely*, *enough for coffee*, *so we must hurry*), which is A0 handled by context rather than hope. The Use stage is built on the same point plus the real countability errors: *a few milk*, *hardly no*, *neither answers were*, *most of students*, *a large number of information*.

cards.title: Quantifiers 2
points: Two new jobs: the **bigger** quantifiers, and the **article** that changes the meaning.
*A few* and *few* look almost the same and mean opposite things.

cards.title: You already know
cards.title_cz: Už znáš — much, many, some, any
points: A2 gave you much, many, a lot of, some, any, no, and the countable split.
Next come the bigger ones, and the meaning the article carries.

rows: a great **deal of** water · a large **number of** people

cards.title: Countable or not
points: Several of these choose their noun. Getting it wrong is the commonest slip.

cards.title: one, two, or more
points: **either** and **neither** are only for **two**. For three or more use **none of**.
**each** looks at them one by one; **every** looks at the whole group.

rows: not one of three or more

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: The first is the important one: the article is not decoration, it is the meaning.

rows: **a few** friends, so I am happy

items.en: There is plenty of time before the train.
items.cz: Do vlaku je spousta času.
items.gap: There is ____ time before the train.
accepts: There's plenty of time before the train.
There is plenty of time before the train.
items.explanation: **plenty of** = more than enough, and it works with uncountable nouns like *time*.
items.explanation_cz: **plenty of** = víc než dost a jde to s nepočitatelnými, jako je *time*.

items.en: She spent a great deal of money on it.
items.cz: Utratila za to spoustu peněz.
accepts: She spent a great deal of money on it.
items.explanation: **a great deal of** goes with UNCOUNTABLE nouns. For countable ones you need *a large number of*.
items.explanation_cz: **a great deal of** jde s NEPOČITATELNÝMI. U počitatelných je *a large number of*.

items.en: A large number of people came to the meeting.
items.cz: Na schůzi přišlo velké množství lidí.
accepts: A large number of people came to the meeting.
items.explanation: **a large number of** goes with COUNTABLE nouns: *people*, not *water*.
items.explanation_cz: **a large number of** jde s POČITATELNÝMI: *people*, ne *water*.

items.en: We waited a couple of hours at the airport.
items.cz: Na letišti jsme čekali pár hodin.
items.gap: We waited ____ hours at the airport.
accepts: We waited a couple of hours at the airport.
items.explanation: **a couple of** = two, or about two.
items.explanation_cz: **a couple of** = dvě, nebo tak dvě.

items.en: Several people asked the same question.
items.cz: Několik lidí se ptalo na totéž.
accepts: Several people asked the same question.
items.explanation: **several** = more than two but not many, and always countable.
items.explanation_cz: **several** = víc než dva, ale ne mnoho, a vždy počitatelné.

items.en: There is hardly any milk left.
items.cz: Skoro žádné mléko nezbylo.
accepts: There's hardly any milk left.
There is hardly any milk left.
items.explanation: **hardly any** = almost none. The sentence stays positive in form.
items.explanation_cz: **hardly any** = skoro žádné. Věta zůstává tvarem kladná.

items.en: None of the shops were open on Sunday.
items.cz: V neděli nebyl otevřený žádný obchod.
items.gap: ____ the shops were open on Sunday.
accepts: None of the shops were open on Sunday.
items.explanation: **none of** works for three or more. *Neither of* is only for exactly two.
items.explanation_cz: **none of** je pro tři a víc. *Neither of* je jen pro přesně dva.

items.en: Most of the students passed the exam.
items.cz: Většina studentů zkoušku udělala.
accepts: Most of the students passed the exam.
items.explanation: Before *the* you need **most of**. Bare *most* comes before a noun with no article.
items.explanation_cz: Před *the* je potřeba **most of**. Holé *most* je před podstatným jménem bez členu.

items.en: Each student gets a different question.
items.cz: Každý student dostane jinou otázku.
accepts: Each student gets a different question.
items.explanation: *Different* means one at a time, so **each**. *Every* looks at the whole group together.
items.explanation_cz: *Different* znamená jeden po druhém, proto **each**. *Every* se dívá na celou skupinu.

items.en: Every single student passed this year.
items.cz: Letos prošel úplně každý student.
accepts: Every single student passed this year.
items.explanation: **every** is the one that takes *single* for emphasis. *Each single* is not English.
items.explanation_cz: **every** bere pro zdůraznění *single*. *Each single* není angličtina.

items.en: Either day is fine for me.
items.cz: Kterýkoli z těch dvou dnů mi vyhovuje.
accepts: Either day is fine for me.
items.explanation: **either** = one of the two, and it is positive. The verb is singular.
items.explanation_cz: **either** = jeden ze dvou a je kladné. Sloveso je v jednotném čísle.

items.en: Neither answer was correct.
items.cz: Ani jedna odpověď nebyla správná.
accepts: Neither answer was correct.
items.explanation: **neither** = not one of the two. It carries the negative by itself.
items.explanation_cz: **neither** = ani jeden ze dvou. Zápor nese samo.

items.en: I have a few friends here, so I am happy.
items.cz: Mám tu pár přátel, takže jsem spokojený.
items.gap: I have ____ friends here, so I am happy.
accepts: I've a few friends here, so I'm happy.
I've a few friends here, so I am happy.
I have a few friends here, so I'm happy.
I have a few friends here, so I am happy.
items.explanation: **a few** = some, and it is POSITIVE. *So I am happy* tells you which one it must be.
items.explanation_cz: **a few** = několik a je to KLADNÉ. *So I am happy* říká, které to musí být.

items.en: He has few friends and feels lonely.
items.cz: Má málo přátel a cítí se osamělý.
items.gap: He has ____ friends and feels lonely.
accepts: He's few friends and feels lonely.
He is few friends and feels lonely.
He has few friends and feels lonely.
items.explanation: **few** without *a* is NEGATIVE: not many, and that is a problem.
items.explanation_cz: **few** bez *a* je ZÁPORNÉ: málo, a je to problém.

items.en: There is a little milk left, enough for coffee.
items.cz: Zbylo trochu mléka, dost na kávu.
items.gap: There is ____ milk left, enough for coffee.
accepts: There's a little milk left, enough for coffee.
There is a little milk left, enough for coffee.
items.explanation: **a little** = some, positive, and uncountable. *Enough for coffee* forces it.
items.explanation_cz: **a little** = trochu, kladné a nepočitatelné. *Enough for coffee* to vynucuje.

items.en: There is little hope of finding it.
items.cz: Naděje, že se to najde, je malá.
items.gap: There is ____ hope of finding it.
accepts: There's little hope of finding it.
There is little hope of finding it.
items.explanation: **little** without *a* is negative: almost none.
items.explanation_cz: **little** bez *a* je záporné: skoro žádná.

items.en: We have a few minutes, so please sit down.
items.cz: Máme pár minut, tak se posaď.
items.gap: We have ____ minutes, so please sit down.
accepts: We've a few minutes, so please sit down.
We have a few minutes, so please sit down.
items.explanation: *So please sit down* means there IS time: **a few**.
items.explanation_cz: *So please sit down* znamená, že čas JE: **a few**.

items.en: Few people understand how it really works.
items.cz: Málokdo chápe, jak to doopravdy funguje.
items.gap: ____ people understand how it really works.
accepts: Few people understand how it really works.
items.explanation: **few** = hardly anybody. Countable, and negative in feeling.
items.explanation_cz: **few** = skoro nikdo. Počitatelné a záporné v pocitu.

items.en: Add a little salt to the soup.
items.cz: Přidej do polévky trochu soli.
accepts: Add a little salt to the soup.
items.explanation: *Salt* is uncountable, and you want some: **a little**.
items.explanation_cz: *Salt* je nepočitatelná a nějakou chceš: **a little**.

items.en: There is little time, so we must hurry.
items.cz: Času je málo, takže musíme spěchat.
items.gap: There is ____ time, so we must hurry.
accepts: There's little time, so we must hurry.
There is little time, so we must hurry.
items.explanation: *So we must hurry* tells you it is not enough: **little**.
items.explanation_cz: *So we must hurry* říká, že to nestačí: **little**.

items.en: A few of the guests stayed until midnight.
items.cz: Pár hostů zůstalo do půlnoci.
accepts: A few of the guests stayed until midnight.
items.explanation: Before *the* you need **a few of**.
items.explanation_cz: Před *the* je potřeba **a few of**.

items.en: Little was said about the accident.
items.cz: O té nehodě se toho moc neřeklo.
accepts: Little was said about the accident.
items.explanation: **little** as the subject means almost nothing was said.
items.explanation_cz: **little** jako podmět znamená, že se skoro nic neřeklo.

items.en: I need a little help with this.
items.cz: Potřebuju s tím trochu pomoct.
accepts: I need a little help with this.
items.explanation: *Help* is uncountable and you are asking for some: **a little**.
items.explanation_cz: *Help* je nepočitatelná a o nějakou žádáš: **a little**.

items.en: He showed little interest in the plan.
items.cz: O ten plán projevil malý zájem.
items.gap: He showed ____ interest in the plan.
accepts: He showed little interest in the plan.
items.explanation: **little** interest = almost none. Dropping the *a* changes the whole meaning.
items.explanation_cz: **little** interest = skoro žádný. Vynechání *a* mění celý význam.

items.en: I have a few friends here, so I am happy.
items.cz: Mám tu pár přátel, takže jsem spokojený.
items.wrong: I have few friends here, so I am happy.
accepts: I've a few friends here, so I'm happy.
I've a few friends here, so I am happy.
I have a few friends here, so I'm happy.
I have a few friends here, so I am happy.
items.explanation: Without *a*, **few** means almost none — which contradicts *so I am happy*. It must be **a few**.
items.explanation_cz: Bez *a* znamená **few** skoro žádné — což si odporuje s *so I am happy*. Musí to být **a few**.

items.en: There is a little milk left, enough for coffee.
items.cz: Zbylo trochu mléka, dost na kávu.
items.wrong: There is a few milk left, enough for coffee.
accepts: There's a little milk left, enough for coffee.
There is a little milk left, enough for coffee.
items.explanation: *Milk* is uncountable, so **a little**, never *a few*.
items.explanation_cz: *Milk* je nepočitatelné, proto **a little**, nikdy *a few*.

items.en: There is hardly any milk left.
items.cz: Skoro žádné mléko nezbylo.
items.wrong: There is hardly no milk left.
accepts: There's hardly any milk left.
There is hardly any milk left.
items.explanation: **hardly any**, never *hardly no*. One negative is enough.
items.explanation_cz: **hardly any**, nikdy *hardly no*. Jeden zápor stačí.

items.en: Neither answer was correct.
items.cz: Ani jedna odpověď nebyla správná.
accepts: Neither answer was correct.
items.explanation: **neither** takes a SINGULAR noun and a singular verb: *neither answer was*.
items.explanation_cz: **neither** má podstatné jméno i sloveso v JEDNOTNÉM čísle: *neither answer was*.

items.en: Most of the students passed the exam.
items.cz: Většina studentů zkoušku udělala.
items.wrong: Most of students passed the exam.
accepts: Most of the students passed the exam.
items.explanation: After **most of** you need *the*: *most of the students*.
items.explanation_cz: Po **most of** je potřeba *the*: *most of the students*.

items.en: A large amount of information was collected.
items.cz: Bylo shromážděno velké množství informací.
items.wrong: A large number of information was collected.
accepts: A large amount of information was collected.
items.explanation: *Information* is uncountable, so it takes **amount**, not *number*.
items.explanation_cz: *Information* je nepočitatelná, proto **amount**, ne *number*.
